description: Key concepts for learning iOS development with Swift and SwiftUI

cards.back: A declarative framework by Apple for building user interfaces across all Apple platforms using Swift code.
A property wrapper that creates a mutable source of truth for a value type, owned by the view. When the value changes, the view re-renders.

cards.front: What is the difference between @State and @Binding?
cards.back: @State owns the data and is the source of truth. @Binding creates a two-way connection to a @State owned by a parent view — it reads and writes but doesn't own.
Apple's modern persistence framework (iOS 17+) that uses Swift macros (@Model) to define schema. It replaces Core Data for new projects.
Marks a Swift class as a SwiftData model, automatically generating persistence support including schema, fetching, and change tracking.
A SwiftUI container that manages a stack-based navigation flow, replacing the deprecated NavigationView. Supports value-based navigation with navigationDestination.
Model-View-ViewModel: a design pattern where the Model holds data, the View displays it, and the ViewModel transforms model data for the view and handles user actions.

cards.front: What is an enum in Swift?
cards.back: A value type that defines a group of related values. Enums in Swift can have associated values, raw values, computed properties, and methods.
